text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.98% today to $129.34, recovering slightly from a steep four-day slide that saw the stock drop nearly $8 (6%) from $133.19 to $125.27. The bounce comes as oil prices stabilized after volatile swings tied to geopolitical uncertainty: Brent crude sits at $114.89 a barrel while US oil is at $96.41, and today's rebound reflects traders cautiously assessing reports that talks may lead to a phased reopening of the Strait of Hormuz—a major choke point for global oil shipments that had tightened supply and pushed prices higher earlier in the week.

The stock's sharp decline over the past two weeks sits against a backdrop of conflicting pressures on the oil market. A Senate vote against ending the Iran war and threats of a diesel export ban are keeping energy prices elevated and volatile, but the prospect of Hormuz reopening has deflated some of the geopolitical premium that had boosted crude prices. Refiners and oil producers face an uncertain demand picture: high diesel prices ($6.51 nationally) are straining customers, yet export restrictions could constrain refiner profits even as crude supply potentially grows.
